retrieval.question: Which APIs expose network access to VSS datapoints?

retrieval.question: How does a data provider convert gathered vehicle data?
retrieval.relevant_quote: Components providing data for leaves in the VSS tree are called  *data-providers*. Technically they are just normal KUKSA clients. Sometimes you will see data-providers to be referred to as "feeders".

lexical_evidence.text: A data-provider will gather some data from a vehicle  using whatever standard or proprietary protocol is needed to access the data. It will then convert the gathered data to the representation defined in a VSS model and provide those standard signals to the VSS server using the VISS or GRPC protocol.
lexical_evidence.title: system-architecture.md
lexical_evidence.name: system-architecture.md

lexical_evidence.text: To sync the desired state in the VSS server to the Vehicle, actuation-providers are used. Similar to the data-provider, an actuation provider also needs to access lower-level Vehicle systems.
lexical_evidence.title: system-architecture.md
lexical_evidence.name: system-architecture.md

lexical_evidence.text: If a provider also supports affecting vehicle systems, based on a desired state being set via the VSS server, it is an *actuation-provider*. Depending on the system design, a provider can be designed to fulfil both the roles as data-provider and actuation-provider.
lexical_evidence.title: system-architecture.md
lexical_evidence.name: system-architecture.md

lexical_evidence.text: To sync the VSS model to the actual state of the vehicle, providers are used. A data-provider might get its information directly from a sensor, from  vehicle busses available to the provider, or from lower parts of the software stack. Historically, data-providers are often called "feeders".

lexical_evidence.name: system-architecture.md

lexical_evidence.text: The [DBC Feeder](https://github.com/eclipse-kuksa/kuksa-can-provider) is an example of a CAN data-provider. It allows mapping of data from a CAN bus based on a DBC description and some mapping rules.

embedding_evidence.text: Another common use case is providing telemetry to the cloud. With cellular networks, being hidden behind NATs or using dynamic IP addresses, the VISS/GRPC pattern of contacting a VSS server is not a suitable. The common pattern is, that the vehicle pushes relevant data, using suitable IoT protocols and potentially dealing with buffering and connection loss. This is the "Cloud Adapter" pattern.
